pr_body:
Previously for iOS builds with persistent workers some required
environment variables like SDKROOT and DEVELOPER_DIR were not passed to
persistent workers when they were spawned. Now we include the
environment variables from the `LocalEnvProvider` that would be used for
fallback builds.

Fixes https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/6223
pr_title: Process persistent worker env before spawning
pr_comment:
See more context about this on https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/6223

I'm not sure if this is the right solution for all workers or not, but I submitted it to start the discussion.

It looks like an alternative solution here would be to move the logic from https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/645a35e1ce0f9f0025e9120399f2e7b77b4841b8/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/exec/apple/XcodeLocalEnvProvider.java#L104

to AppleConfiguration https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/645a35e1ce0f9f0025e9120399f2e7b77b4841b8/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/rules/apple/AppleConfiguration.java#L130-L134

I'm not sure what other implications that would have

I don't know enough about how workers work, so I'll just have to ask a question that hopefully @philwo can answer.

`DEVELOPER_DIR` is controlled based on the version of Xcode currently selected (passing `--xcode_version` to Bazel) and based on wherever the `xcode-locator` tool detects those Xcode installations to be, and `SDKROOT` is controlled IIRC by the `--apple_platform_type` flag, which can be past manually but is typically used via a configuration transition from `ios_application`, `watchos_application`, etc.

If we have a persistent worker that spans multiple compilation actions, are we guaranteed that actions with different `(--xcode_version, --apple_platform_type)` pairs will be sent to workers that have been launched with the correct environments? We don't want a situation where a worker is launched with an `iPhoneSimulator` SDK root but it gets sent compilation actions for watchOS libraries, for example.

We likely already have this problem. If you see in my original post here https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/6223 the variables that are currently passed, they contain both the SDK and the Xcode version already. I'm not sure if those are ready anywhere by Bazel or Xcode's toolchain but if they are the persistent workers would already be specific to these.


--
Keith Smiley

Yes, this is guaranteed. The environment with which a worker was launched
is part of its WorkerKey. If you have two workers of the same kind but
different environments, Bazel will launch independent instances and route
to them correctly.
